_meta.note: Canonical schema for .planning/config.json. Source of truth for keys, types, enums, and defaults. Validated by bin/config.mjs; the cad-config walk reads each setting's question and value explanations from it (see `walk`). `src` is CONFIG-LAYER SCOPE, not enum provenance: [repo] = settable in either layer; [global] = the user-global layer only, and a repo layer setting it is stripped at the merge and named in the read face's warnings (bin/lib/global-only-keys.mjs, cross-checked against this field by self-verify in both directions); absent = repo-settable. `repo_only` is a DIFFERENT and much narrower marker than `src`, and the two are read separately: present and `true` means only that repository's own .planning/config.json can set the key, so bin/config.mjs REFUSES a write aimed at the user-global layer at write time rather than stripping it at the merge; absent means either layer, which is every other key. The test it encodes, for a maintainer deciding whether a new key qualifies: would a user-global value AUTHORIZE a change to a repository that never opted in? If yes the key is `repo_only`; a key that merely has a sensible per-repo value is not.
_meta.types: bool | int | string | string_or_null | enum | array_string | array_enum. int accepts an optional 'min'. enum/array_enum carry 'values'. `grammar` is an OPTIONAL further narrowing of a value whose type already passed, naming one predicate in the frozen GRAMMARS registry of bin/lib/config-value.mjs: the type says what kind of value this is, the grammar says which of those values this key serves. It is evaluated at the write face (set/check) and over a whole file (validate), a null value skips it because null means the question was never asked, and a marker naming a predicate the registry does not hold is an error rather than a silent pass - a key claiming a grammar nothing enforces is the failure the marker exists to prevent.
_meta.walk: OPTIONAL per-key fields that carry the /cad-config walk's text, so the walk and any other reader (a config panel) take it from this one file. `question` is the sentence the walk asks, and its presence marks the key as part of the walk; a key without it is not asked about. `section` names the group the key sits under and `position` is its 1-based place in the walk, which is not schema order. `explain` is a list of `{value, text}` entries, one per selectable answer: `value` keeps its real JSON type (a string, `true`, `false` or `null`) because an object keyed by value could only hold strings, and `text` is optional, so a bare entry is an answer with no gloss. Every explained value must be one the key accepts. `hint` is a free-typed shape (a number, a shell command, a path, a comma list) and is never a selectable value, so a reader must not offer it as an option. `purpose` stays the key's reference text and is not the question. `bin/config.mjs keys --walk` returns only the keys that hold a question, in `position` order.

workflow.max_plan_tasks.purpose: Task ceiling PER PLAN, not per phase - a phase needing more capacity gets MORE PLANS, sequential where they share files, and `## PHASE TOO BIG` is returned only when no number of plans of that size can deliver the phase, which is a statement about the PHASE's scope and not about task count. The ceiling the planner is given up front, so an oversized plan is split rather than silently built. Re-decided 2026-08-17 against both of its forces and landing on 8, unchanged: cold-prefix cost - `weight.mjs resident` puts the executor's fixed dispatch prefix at 12,488 bytes, about 2% of a measured executor dispatch, so what an extra plan re-buys is the cold pass over the plan and the phase's artifacts rather than the prefix - and context risk - 15 executor checkpoints of 21 on this repo's `.planning/trace.jsonl`, every one of them from a plan already under this ceiling. v3.8.6:design-notes/dd-plan-task-ceiling.md carries the dated arithmetic
workflow.max_plan_tasks.question: Task ceiling PER PLAN; a phase needing more capacity gets more plans, sequential where they share files. Counted at `check_size` by `planning.mjs plan-size`. Re-decided 2026-08-17 against both of its forces and landing on 8, unchanged: cold-prefix cost (the executor's fixed dispatch prefix is 12,488 bytes, about 2% of a measured executor dispatch, so an extra plan re-buys the cold pass rather than the prefix) and context risk (15 executor checkpoints of 21 in `.planning/trace.jsonl`, every one from a plan already under this ceiling); arithmetic: `v3.8.6:design-notes/dd-plan-task-ceiling.md`

workflow.max_plan_bytes.purpose: Byte ceiling on what a SINGLE plan's `files:` frontmatter declares, measured as the sum of the on-disk sizes of those declared paths - PER PLAN and not per phase, the same reading workflow.max_plan_tasks carries, so a plan over it is split into MORE PLANS rather than shrunk in place. Those declared paths are what an executor dispatch is handed, and on one measured PLAN-1.md they were about 90% of a 70,554-token dispatch while nothing measured them against anything. A crossing is REPORTED and nothing is refused: plan-size report only (`bin/planning.mjs`), which workflows/plan.md hands the resolved value at its `check_size` step as `plan-size --max-bytes`; no dispatch path, agent frontmatter key or spawn seam consults it, so an over-ceiling plan is still planned and still executed. That is planning.max_capture_bullets's disposition and for its reason - the user may have authorized the full scope one step earlier, and a check that refused what they just authorized would be arguing with them. The default is the 75th percentile of the declared-byte distribution over this repository's 43 archived plans rounded UP to the next 25,000 (p25 207,298, p50 401,107, p75 667,580, p90 933,283, max 1,282,083, measured 2026-08-26; it fires on 10 of the 43), which is the derivation rule the six workflow.max_dispatch_tokens.* keys already state; references/config-reach.md carries the reach row
workflow.max_plan_bytes.question: Byte ceiling PER PLAN on what its `files:` frontmatter declares, summed over the on-disk sizes of those paths - the read set an executor dispatch is handed. Measured at `check_size` by `planning.mjs plan-size --max-bytes`, which reports the crossing and refuses nothing; the remedy is more plans, as it is for `workflow.max_plan_tasks`. The default is the 75th percentile of the declared-byte distribution across this repository's 43 archived plans rounded up to the next 25,000 (p75 667,580, max 1,282,083, measured 2026-08-26; it fires on 10 of the 43), the derivation rule the six `workflow.max_dispatch_tokens.*` keys already state

git.forge_provider.purpose: Which forge hosts this repository's issue tracker, resolved ONCE at project setup by /cad-new-project or /cad-adopt and read at land time in place of any host detection: bin/issue-check.mjs picks its provider row from this value rather than classifying the origin URL, so a repository that temporarily loses its remote does not silently change behaviour. Spelled with the same vocabulary bin/lib/issue-decision.mjs's HOST_TABLE uses for its rows. null means unasked - the setup step has not run or the user has not picked a provider yet. Settable in either config layer: naming which forge you use is a preference, and it authorizes nothing on a repository that never named ITSELF - binding a call to a repository is git.forge_repo's job, and that key is repo_only.

git.auto_close.purpose: Opt-in end-to-end close: cad-milestone/cad-land run audit -> tag -> PR -> merge -> reset with no per-step prompts, halting on a surviving blocker/high risk_surface finding. It runs only when both config layers set it: the repository's .planning/config.json AND the user-global config must both be true, and either alone does nothing. A user-global value cannot authorize a repository that never opted in (D-08), and a committed repository value cannot authorize an unattended push on a machine whose user never opted in (D-02). Every reader goes through lib/repo-auto-close.mjs's both-layer read: git-publish.mjs publish and authorized, land-cleanup.mjs gate, and /cad-land step 3 and /cad-milestone step 7, which both branch on git-publish.mjs authorized.

planning.max_capture_bullets.purpose: Bound on the SUBSTANTIVE walked bullets .planning/CAPTURE.md may hold - the Todos, Seeds and Notes count with the `- None.` placeholder excluded, which is what `planning.mjs capture-check` reports. A crossing is REPORTED and nothing is refused, the same consequence workflow.max_dispatch_tokens.* carries and for the same reason: capture-check report only (`bin/planning.mjs`), no writer consults it, so /cad-capture and /cad-execute's open items keep filing at a queue that is over. The default is this repository's own live figure rounded up - 30 substantive walked bullets measured 2026-08-25 after the hand sweep - so the bound sits ABOVE a healthy tree and fires on GROWTH rather than on arrival, because a bound that reddens the day it ships teaches its reader to ignore it. What it is for: the hand sweep took this queue to zero on 2026-08-08 and it regrew to 276 walked items in sixteen days, because nothing measured it against anything. references/config-reach.md carries the reach row

review.triggers.risk_surface.surfaces.purpose: Which of the eight risk surfaces the risk-surface review fires on - a heuristic match in a category outside this list does NOT fire the trigger. Left unset it means all eight, and it is also the UNANSWERED state: the first risk_surface fire on a project that has not answered runs the structural scan and asks once, then writes the answer here. There is deliberately no default array - a default of all eight would make "the user chose everything" indistinguishable from "nobody has answered"

explain.text: all eight, and the first fire asks once

review.triggers.risk_surface.waive_routi.purpose: Which surfaces may NOT raise this project's plan-time risk floor. The floor does exactly two things - it makes the plan review blocking and it turns the deep-verify pass on - and naming a surface here withholds BOTH for that surface. It waives neither review itself: the blocking risk_surface review still fires on the actual diff, and this key cannot turn it off. It moves no role's model and no role's start rung, because the floor does not move those either. Every waiver applied is named in the resolve's `reason` with the surface and the file it would have raised on. A surface that is NOT named still raises: waiving `secrets` on a phase that also touches `destructive` still gets the blocking plan review and the deep pass. Left unset it waives nothing, which is a different state from an empty answer for the same reason its `surfaces` sibling has no default array
review.triggers.risk_surface.waive_routi.question: Which risky-code categories should stop raising the bar on a phase that touches them? (risk_surface only) - a category picked here stops making the plan review blocking and stops turning the deep-verify pass on; it moves no role's model and no role's rung, and it cannot turn the `risk_surface` review off

explain.text: nothing is waived

review.triggers.risk_surface.waive_routi.hint: the same eight as `surfaces`, listed because this row is where a reader meets them. A category you leave out still raises both. Every category actually waived is named in the routing decision's `reason`
